questions.q: Which earlier chapter's ideas -- management groups, subscription vending, and choosing boundaries by blast radius -- did Lesson 29's design directly apply?
options: Chapter 7, Presenting and Defending an Architecture
Chapter 2, Landing Zones and Multi-Account Design
Chapter 6, Architecture Decision Records and Documentation
Chapter 1, Enterprise Cloud Architecture Principles
questions.explain: Chapter 2 is the direct source of the management-group and subscription-boundary ideas Lesson 29 applied to Harlow Creek Logistics.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what was the real cause of Prairiewind Underwriters' outage from Lesson 31?
options: A review-process failure -- a checklist shaped around application tiers with no line item for shared infrastructure -- not a purely technical one
A coding error in the claims-processing application
An insufficient Azure Firewall throughput tier
A missing backup of the claims database
questions.explain: The applications failed over correctly; the gap was that the review process never asked about the shared network layer's own disaster recovery plan.

questions.q: What are the four courses that make up the completed Advanced Specialization stage?
options: Networking, Linux & Cloud Fundamentals; Azure Administration; AWS Administration; Identity & Security
How IT Teams Work; Python & PowerShell Automation; Cloud Infrastructure Deployment Capstone; Identity & Security
Terraform/Bicep IaC; Docker/Kubernetes; Cloud Operations/FinOps; Enterprise Cloud Architecture & Advanced Capstone
Advanced Platform Engineering; Hybrid/Multi-Cloud Architecture; AI Cloud Infrastructure; Advanced SRE
questions.explain: Those four courses -- IaC, containers, cloud ops/FinOps, and this capstone -- make up the Advanced Specialization stage that this lesson closes out.

questions.q: How many courses are in the Expert Specialization stage that follows this course, and in what order must they be taken?
options: Three courses, in a strict required sequence
Four courses, which can be taken in any order since they build on Advanced Specialization but not on each other
Five courses, taken two at a time
Four courses, but only after completing a separate certification exam
questions.explain: Expert Specialization has four courses -- platform engineering/GitOps, hybrid/multi-cloud, AI infrastructure, and advanced SRE -- that can be taken in any order.

questions.q: Which Expert Specialization course does this lesson say extends this chapter's landing zone and hub-and-spoke thinking across cloud providers and on-premises environments?
options: AI Cloud Infrastructure, GPU Computing & MLOps
Advanced Platform Engineering, GitOps & CI/CD
Advanced Site Reliability Engineering, Disaster Recovery & Resilience
Hybrid & Multi-Cloud Enterprise Architecture
questions.explain: Hybrid & Multi-Cloud Enterprise Architecture is named as the course that takes this chapter's single-tenant landing zone ideas and extends them across providers and on-premises environments.
